subject: Dedicated capacity validation: GPU tradeoffs & next-step plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.r@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.b@brightwave.ai>; SRE Team <sre@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.f@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.o@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed validation plan (dedicated capacity)

Thanks for the time today, Evan — good conversation. Quick recap of the BrightWave constraints and the draft plan so we can align on next steps: 

Key targets you outlined
- P95 end-to-end latency (streaming enabled): target <= 220 ms for short-form responses (~64 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: 250 complete requests/min during business hours; ability to handle 2x bursts to 500 r/min for up to 10 minutes.
- Concurrent streams: typical concurrency 45–60 active streams, peaks ~120.
- Token streaming requirement: low-latency token flushes (partial tokens every ~50-100ms).
- Availability: preference for Dedicated with private VPC for compliance reasons.

What we propose for validation (high-level)
1) Environment: private Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with isolated VPC.
2) GPU candidates: H100 (best raw throughput), A100 80GB (balanced memory/throughput), L4x2 (cost-optimized) — we'll benchmark all three with your sample workload.
3) Workload replay: run a synthetic replay of 48 hours of representative traffic (anonymized payloads you provide) with your observed concurrency and arrival distribution.
4) Metrics: measure p50/p95/p99 latency per-token and end-to-end, throughput (reqs/min and tokens/sec), GPU util, and tail stalls due to KV cache warmup.
5) Streaming config: test both aggressive flush (50ms) and default (100ms) to measure perceptible latency differences.
6) Success criteria: p95 <= 220ms for streaming baseline; tail p99 < 450ms; no dropped streams under 120 concurrent sessions.

Action items / asks from BrightWave
- Provide a 2–4 hour anonymized sample trace (JSONL) showing request timestamps, prompt lengths, and expected stream behavior.
- Confirm whether any prompts will require long-context (>=16k tokens) which affects model choice and KV memory.
- Procurement contact to sign the SOW & temporary test IP allowlist for test window.

Internal next steps (we'll handle)
- Diego: run initial microbenchmarks across GPU candidates and produce a bench summary.
- Karthik: design the replay script to match their arrival distribution and streaming semantics.
- Grace: coordinate SOW and procurement paperwork; propose test dates.

I'll schedule a 30–45 minute pre-test sync once we have the sample trace and a signed SOW. Thanks — Aisha

--

Thanks, Aisha — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We'll scrub the sample trace for PII and deliver a 3-hour anonymized trace by EOD Monday. It will include token counts and timestamps. 
- Private VPC is non-negotiable due to internal policy. We need the validation pool to be in our Azure tenancy or connected via a secure peering. Can you confirm Redwood supports a VPC peering test in a partner cloud region (we're in us-west-2, Azure)?
- Regarding GPUs: we prefer to start with H100 if it's materially better for streaming tail latency; if H100 delta is small vs A100 we'll consider the latter for cost reasons.
- Budget ask: can you provide a ballpark for a 4-week reserved validation window (including two benchmark passes) on Dedicated for each GPU candidate so procurement can start internal approvals?

Evan

Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + proposed validation plan (dedicated capacity)

Hi all — attaching a short benchmark primer and initial microbench PDF (attached: gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf). Key technical notes from our side: 

- Measurement approach: we will run both latency-first (small batch, synchronous) and throughput-first (larger batch, token-level concurrency) passes. For streaming, synchronous batching tends to increase tail latencies, so we'll run a streaming-optimized pass with batch_size=1 and async writes to the stream.
- Batch/concurrency guidance: start with batch_size 1–4 for streaming (to minimize per-token latency) and batch_size 8–16 for throughput-only tests. Use concurrency targets of 50 / 100 / 150 to characterize scaling points.
- KV cache warm-up: cold-starts add measurable p99 tail; we'll include a warm-up phase and measure differences with and without prefix caching.
- Resource recommendation: for your requested SLOs I expect H100 to hit p95 targets more comfortably at peak concurrency; A100 will be close but may need slightly higher reserved throughput or more instances. L4x2 could be cost-efficient for low-memory models but will struggle on long-context cases.

Artifacts and where to upload sample traces: we created a secure pre-test bucket and a checklist doc (pre-test-checklist.md). Please upload to: https://secure-s3.redwood.ai/brightwave-tests/RDW-2345 (we'll share an IP allowlist once procurement completes).

I'll run a quick smoke test once we have the sample trace and post the initial numbers within 48 hours of receipt. 

- Diego

Thanks — Aisha

Those dates look fine. A couple final asks before we kick off: 

1) Pre-test checklist & success criteria in a one-page doc we can attach to our change window request (helps our SOC).
2) A concise runbook for the test that lists expected IPs, ports, and rollback triggers if we see production-impacting signals.

We will upload the anonymized trace by Monday EOD as promised. Procurement will review the SOW; I asked them to route it immediately. 

Success criteria for our internal acceptance (summary):
- Streaming p95 <= 220 ms for typical short responses (64 tokens).
- End-to-end session stability: no more than 1% dropped streams under 120 concurrent sessions.
- Tail p99 < 450 ms.

If Redwood can provide the one-page checklist and the runbook link by Aug 21, we will mark the change window and proceed. Looking forward to the test.

— Evan
